newsitem.title: UK: British economy grows 3.4 percent in 2nd quarter.
newsitem.headline: British economy grows 3.4 percent in 2nd quarter.

text.p: Britain's economy grew an annual 3.4 percent in the second quarter of 1997, official figures showed on Friday.

Economic growth was 0.9 percent in the second quarter over the first. The data were in line with analysts' expectations but underlined the above-trend strength of the economy and maintained the pressure for higher interest rates.
British economy grows 3.4 percent in 2nd quarter

"The figures ... still confirm that the economy is growing more strongly than the Bank of England would want," said Nick Stamenkovic of DKB International. "It does increase the pressure for a rate hike."
Rates have been increased three times since Labour's May 1 election victory to 6.75 percent to stem inflationary pressures in Britain's booming economy.
Sterling, boosted above three marks by expectations of higher rates, was little changed by the data but shares eased further.
